current.text: Charlotte got him from Phoenix in a trade, along with Royce O'Neale, for Miles Bridges.
He is projected as Charlotte's sixth man. The projected starters are White, Knueppel, Miller, Reid and Diabaté.
He starts while Kon Knueppel is out.
He would also start if Brandon Miller misses games, but the expert is not sure that will happen.
His role should be smaller than it was in Phoenix. He could still get about 27 minutes off the bench.
His shot volume should drop from last season's high level. Experts expect better efficiency, and his FG% could bounce back. He should help as a secondary creator off the bench.

Experts disagree on his draft value. The newest call says Yahoo ranks him too low at 160. It puts him at 100 to 115 (rounds 10 to 11) as a late-round swing, but says not to boost him much. Other experts see a low ceiling and would not draft him.
With a March 28 end, Charlotte plays 4, 3 and 4 games in our playoff weeks. It has only 13 back-to-backs, the league minimum.

durable.text: He can play the two, three and four and can handle the ball.
He plays bigger than his size and drives downhill, and that has worn his body down.
He is older, has soft tissue problems and carries injury risk. One expert thinks he has peaked and is on the back nine of his career.
Most of his value comes from threes, with small help in FT% and steals. His FG% is weak for his position.

note: Yahoo ranks him 187 and ESPN 157, and both value him at 0 USD. That puts him outside our 144 drafted players, so at most he is a 1 USD late pick in a punt FG% build that wants threes, FT% and some steals. In the first weeks, check how many minutes he gets while Knueppel is out and whether his FG% recovers from last season's 40.3% on lower volume. If he plays about 27 minutes as a starter, pick him up off waivers.
